global_all_C_conjecture_status: Unresolved; no counterexample found in the retained finite diagnostics. The theorem below is local in C for each fixed interior(A,B).

definitions.model: p(x)=A+B cos x+C sin x, B^2+C^2<=min(A,1-A)^2.
definitions.oracle: V(A,B,C)=sup_w inf_{physical(a,b)} integral kl(p(x)||a+b cos x) w(dx), with natural logarithms.
definitions.reflection: Write z=cos x in[-1,1], s=sqrt(1-z^2), and p_minus=A+Bz-C s,p_plus=A+Bz+C s, taking C>0 without loss of generality.
definitions.capacity: R(z,C)=kl(p_minus||q_c)=kl(p_plus||q_c). Its achieving plus-arm weight is omega=(q_c-p_minus)/(p_plus-p_minus), strictly between0 and1 for distinct interior endpoints.
definitions.zero_extension: At C=0 or z=+/-1 define q_c=A+Bz and R=0 by continuity. For fixed interior(A,B), q_c and R are analytic in z and C^2 on a neighborhood of[-1,1] times{0}.

theorem.assumptions: Fix0<A<1 and |B|<min(A,1-A). There exists epsilon(A,B)>0 such that for every0<|C|<epsilon(A,B), the model is physical and the following statements hold.
theorem.one_dimensional_exact_value: V(A,B,C)=max_{-1<=z<=1} R(z,C). The maximizer z*(C) is unique and interior in this weak-signal neighborhood.
theorem.optimal_design: Use x*=arccos z*, its reflection -x*, and weights omega(z*,C),1-omega(z*,C). For negative C swap the arm labels/weights as needed.
theorem.explicit_tangent_null: Let b*=partial_z q_c(z*,C), a*=q_c(z*,C)-b*z*. Then q*(x)=a*+b* cos x is physically feasible and kl(p(x)||q*(x))<=R(z*,C) for EVERY real x.
theorem.one_sided_extension: The same value/design/certificate hold if the null is enlarged to the opposite physical sign C_null<=0 for C>0, or C_null>=0 for C<0.
theorem.claim_boundary: This is an oracle information-design theorem. It does not give a computable uniform epsilon, paid-learning policy, finite95%/1% cost gain, or novelty/SOTA conclusion.

proof_steps.claim: Every reflection pair yields a capacity lower bound.
proof_steps.argument: The logit secant lies strictly between logit(p_minus) and logit(p_plus), so p_minus<q_c<p_plus. Its definition makes the two endpoint KLs equal. With omega=(q_c-p_minus)/(p_plus-p_minus), the weighted Bernoulli KL is minimized at the mixture mean q_c. A constant null(a,b)=(q_c,0) is physical, so this two-arm design has exact null-information value R. Consequently V>=max_z R.

proof_steps.claim: The limiting one-dimensional objective has a unique nondegenerate interior maximum.
proof_steps.argument: Let p0=A+Bz, v=A(1-A), d=v-B^2, e=B(1-2A). Because(A+/-B)(1-A-/+B)>0, d>|e|. The limiting objective is h(z)=(1-z^2)/(2 p0(1-p0)). Its reciprocal apart from2 is w(z)=p0(1-p0)/(1-z^2)=B^2+(d+ez)/(1-z^2). Its derivative has numerator e(1+z^2)+2dz, with exactly one root inside(-1,1): z0=-e/(d+sqrt(d^2-e^2)); this formula also gives0 when e=0. At the root d2w/dz2=2 sqrt(d^2-e^2)/(1-z0^2)^2>0. Thus h has a unique strict nondegenerate global maximum z0; h(+/-1)=0.

proof_steps.claim: The capacity maximizer persists analytically for small C.
proof_steps.argument: The strict interior margin of p0 on[-1,1] makes f analytic uniformly around every p0. The entropy secant has an even power series in C sqrt(1-z^2); hence q_c=p0+C^2 g(z)+O(C^4) and R=C^2 h(z)+O(C^4), including derivatives in z on[-1,1]. Here g(z)=(1-z^2)(2p0-1)/(6p0(1-p0)). Therefore R/C^2 extends analytically in(z,C^2). The implicit-function theorem at the nondegenerate maximum gives z*(C)=z0+O(C^2), analytic in C^2. Uniform convergence and the nonzero derivative of h off any neighborhood of z0 make this the unique global maximum for all sufficiently small C.

proof_steps.claim: The tangent null is physical and matches two stationary equal-height contacts.
proof_steps.argument: Since q_c=p0+O(C^2) with its first z derivative, the tangent coefficients satisfy(a*,b*)=(A,B)+O(C^2). The fixed strict null margin |B|<min(A,1-A) guarantees physical feasibility for small C. At z*, the line q_t(z)=a*+b*z has both the same value and same first derivative as q_c. Thus F_plus(z)=kl(p_plus(z)||q_t(z)) and F_minus(z)=kl(p_minus(z)||q_t(z)) satisfy F_plus(z*)=F_minus(z*)=R(z*,C) and partial_z F_plus(z*)=partial_z F_minus(z*)=partial_z R(z*,C)=0.

proof_steps.claim: These two contacts are GLOBAL KL maxima, not just tangencies.
proof_steps.argument: Choose a closed neighborhood J of z0 strictly inside(-1,1), small enough that d2h/dz2<=-lambda<0 on J. On J, F_plus/C^2 and F_minus/C^2 converge to h in the C^2 norm as C->0; this means convergence of functions and two z derivatives, NOT an O(C^2) convergence rate. Hence each F branch is strictly concave on J for sufficiently small C, and its stationary point z* is its unique maximum there. Globally on[-1,1], both normalized branches converge uniformly to h: Taylor expansion of KL uses p_plus/minus-q_t=+/-C sqrt(1-z^2)+O(C^2), uniformly including endpoints. The strict global gap h(z0)-max_{z outside J}h(z)>0 therefore implies F_plus(z),F_minus(z)<R(z*,C) outside J once C is small enough. This proves the uniform all-angle bound.

proof_steps.claim: The upper certificate matches the design lower bound.
proof_steps.argument: For every distribution w over angles, the same physical null q* gives inf_null integral KL<=integral KL(p||q*)<=R(z*,C). Combined with Step1 this proves equality and the optimal design.

proof_steps.claim: The opposite-sign extension has the same value.
proof_steps.argument: At the reflected angles, any opposite-sign null has ordered rates q_plus<=q_minus. Weighted KL to the true ordered p_plus>p_minus is minimized over this order cone by pooling at their weighted mean q_c. The constant physical null attains it. The upper bound still uses the same C_null=0 tangent null, so the sandwich remains exact.

closed_asymptotics.weight: omega=1/2+C sqrt(1-z0^2)(2(A+Bz0)-1)/[12(A+Bz0)(1-A-Bz0)]+O_{A,B}(C^3), for the plus endpoint when C>0.
closed_asymptotics.null: b*=B+C^2 partial_z g(z0)+O(C^4), a*=A+C^2[g(z0)-z0 partial_z g(z0)]+O(C^4).
closed_asymptotics.nonuniformity: All O constants and the existence neighborhood depend on fixed(A,B). The proof is not uniform when |B| approaches min(A,1-A) while C also approaches0; the limiting maximizer may approach z=+/-1.

other_exact_cases.B_zero: For B=0 and any physical C, p(x) lies in[A-|C|,A+|C|]. Choose the Bernoulli capacity center of these endpoints as a constant null. KL is convex in p, so every angle is dominated by the two endpoint KLs. The reflected PSR pair+/-pi/2 with capacity weights is globally optimal, including boundary endpoints by continuity.
other_exact_cases.A_half: The previously proved operator-concavity theorem gives global exact optimality of equally weighted PSR for A=1/2 and every physical B,C.
other_exact_cases.C_zero: The model is a null; the oracle value is0.

global_conjecture_reduction.two_support_kkt: If a positive-information two-support design has an INTERIOR minimizing affine null, KKT gives sum_i g_i=0 and sum_i z_i g_i=0, g_i=w_i(q_i-p_i)/[q_i(1-q_i)]. Distinct z_i force both g_i=0 and zero information. Thus such a two-support solution must have the same cosine at both angles, hence be a reflection pair. This does not exclude three or more supports or a boundary null.
global_conjecture_reduction.sufficient_curvature_lemma: Let R*=max_z R(z,C). Define ell_R(p) and u_R(p) as the lower and upper endpoints of{q:kl(p||q)<=R}. If L(z)=ell_R*(p_plus(z)) is concave and U(z)=u_R*(p_minus(z)) is convex globally, then L<=U and at a capacity maximum they meet. Their common tangent line lies above L and below U, giving the full conjecture immediately.
global_conjecture_reduction.exact_lower_inverse_derivatives: For p>q=ell_R(p), put K=q(1-q)[logit(p)-logit(q)]/(p-q). Then d ell_R/dp=K and d2 ell_R/dp2={1/[p(1-p)]-2K/[q(1-q)]+[p/q^2+(1-p)/(1-q)^2]K^2} q(1-q)/(p-q). Consequently d2L/dz2=(d2 ell_R/dp2)(B-Cz/sqrt(1-z^2))^2-(d ell_R/dp) C/(1-z^2)^(3/2). The upper branch follows by probability complementation.
global_conjecture_reduction.remaining_gap: The required global curvature sign has not been proved from physicality at R*. Joint convexity of KL alone is insufficient, and the corresponding claim fails for unrestricted large radii. The prior operator proof uses a normalized trace-one state with A=1/2 and does not directly establish the general tangent-null claim.
